text:
Mira: :rotating_light: High error rate on /v1/generate from a handful of customer tenants, noticed spike ~10:05 UTC. 5xxs and token latency climbing.
Joel: Oncall paging? I can take a look, pinging infra and runtime.
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered for infra-incidents (severity: high) — oncall: Joel.
Sam: Logs show KV cache keys for rope/ntk sliding-window exploded. A single request pattern created ~1.2M new prefixes in last 3m.
Carla: Wow. Any hotfix we can try without redeploying models? Maybe disable sliding-window at runtime.
Mira: Yes — we have a runtime feature flag: runtime.set feature rope_sliding_window=false. Also can throttle continuous batching limits. Both are low-risk.
Joel: I'm on the pager. Starting with safe actions: 1) set sliding-window off, 2) reduce continuous batch max_size from 4096 -> 512, 3) purge kv prefixes for rope_* older than 30m. I'm coordinating with Sam.
Sam: Command snippets:

```
# disable feature flag for all inference nodes
redwoodctl runtime-flag set rope.sliding_window false --scope inference

# reduce continuous batching size
redwoodctl config set inference.continuous_batch.max_size 512 --env prod

# purge rope keys older than 30m (dry-run first)
admin-cli kv keys --prefix rope_ntk_ | grep -E "rope_ntk_" | xargs -n 100 admin-cli kv purge --dry-run
```

Joel: Running disable flag now.
ops-bot: Applying runtime flag rope.sliding_window=false to 24 nodes: started.
Joel: Flag applied, waiting for nodes to reconnect. Watching error rate.
Carla: After flag flip, error rate dipped by ~40% in 30s but still higher than baseline.
Mira: Proceeding to reduce batch size. Sam is staging config change.
Sam: Applying batch config change via rollout: set max_size=512 and propagate to inference service groups A,B,C with 30s stagger.
ops-bot: Rollout triggered: inference.continuous_batch.max_size=512 -> groups A,B,C.
Joel: Batch size change live. Latency improved, error count trending down. But KV namespace still growing — we should purge stale prefixes.
Sam: Doing purge now. Running in small batches to avoid thundering herd:

```
admin-cli kv keys --prefix rope_ntk_ --older-than 1800 | split -l 1000 -d --filter="xargs -n 100 admin-cli kv purge" -
```

Carla: Note — purging may temporarily increase CPU due to compaction. We'll do few hundred thousand keys at a time.
Mira: Customer impact tracking: 12 customers experienced 5xxs from 10:04 to 10:18 UTC. Major impact window ~14m.
Joel: I'm posting a status to #general and CS. Drafting a short summary.
Joel: Status update to CS: "We saw a cache blowup tied to long-context rope scaling (NTK/YaRN sliding-window) causing KV explosion and backpressure on inference nodes. Hotfixes applied: disabled sliding-window, reduced continuous batch max_size, purged stale KV prefixes. Error rates returning to baseline. Oncall will monitor and follow up with postmortem." :white_check_mark:
Carla: Any evidence it was a single tenant or widespread traffic pattern?
Sam: Initial spike originated from a single customer deploying long-context feature with aggressive sliding-window (window stride small -> many unique keys). But others were impacted due to shared inference pool and cache saturation.
Mira: Immediate mitigation looks good. We should schedule a dedicated rollback guard — re-enable only after we deploy a caching-shape fix.
Joel: Agreed. I'll keep the feature flag off and monitor for 1h. Handoff: I'm due to hand off to Mira at 12:00 UTC — Mira will be primary after that.
Mira: Confirmed. I'll take over monitoring and write the initial incident note for postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident declared: "KV cache blowup from rope sliding-window; mitigation applied" — severity: high — incident id: IN-20260302-87
Sam: Follow-up actions I'm adding:
- Add guardrails to sliding-window feature to enforce NTK caps per-request
- Add rate-limits and prefix-scope limits to KV to avoid global explosion
- Add a presubmit test that simulates high-NTK requests
- Improve telemetry: surface per-tenant new-key-rate to detect blowups earlier

Carla: Also recommend an autoscale policy change: when key-creation-rate spikes, throttle new sessions to protect shared pools.
Joel: Handing off monitoring to Mira now. My oncall notes: keep rope.sliding_window=false, batch.max_size=512, continue purging old keys until growth rate normalizes (<1000 new keys/min across cluster). If growth persists escalate to infra lead.
Mira: Taking over. I'll update the incident doc and start a postmortem draft. Adding customer impact details and timeline.
Carla: Any regression window for customers to revert? Some customers may restart their clients to clear local prefixes — we should coordinate with CS for remediation steps.
Mira: I'll include remediation steps for CS: 1) restart client process, 2) delay sliding-window usage, 3) request support if they need cache-level wipes.
Joel: One more note: we should avoid large immediate purges during peak traffic; we did small batches and that worked. Marking that as a lesson learned.
incident-bot: Ops note: a follow-up maintenace window suggested 2026-03-03 02:00 UTC for permanent fixes.
Mira: Closing thread for active mitigation; will re-open for postmortem. Thanks everyone. :pray:
